text:
anya: Kicking off pragmatic bring-up for Archon-13B (aiming int8 first, int4 smoke later). Need a concise perf sweep plan: throughput, latency, batching, ctx sweeps, and warmup profiles. Who can own the runbook?

matt: I can drive the throughput/latency jobs. My plan: 1) baseline hosted config (no caching), 2) batching grid, 3) ctx-length sweep. Targets: p50 < 60ms (single-token), p99 < 400ms for 1k ctx. Will add canary for dedicated later. :+1:

jess: I'll take quant/quality regressions and eval sets. Suggest we run two eval suites: "small-conv" (chatty prompts) and "doc-summarize" (long contexts) to catch hallucination/format regressions.

sam: Quick note on warmup: we should run a KV-prefix warmup with 3x typical requests to fill cache before measuring tail latencies. Also measure cold-start (empty cache) vs warm.

anya: Good. Let's pick concrete parameter grid. Matt, propose numbers and I'll wire up dashboards and alerts.

matt: Proposed grid: batching=[1,4,8,16], tokens_per_request=128 (throughput), ctx=[512,1024,2048,8192], concurrency=[1,4,8]. For each cell capture p50/p95/p99, throughput (tokens/s), GPU util, and memory headroom. Prioritize batch sizes 1 and 4 for latency SLOs.

jess: For quant smoke: run int8 baseline then int4 fallback. Quality check: run evals after each quant step and compare Rouge/BLEU + embedding-sim delta. Flag if embedding-sim drops > 0.06 or Rouge drops > 2.

sam: Add these operational checks to runbook: 1) confirm kernel selection (cuBLAS vs custom) 2) check dev mem fragmentation 3) ensure fp16 fallback path present.

perf-bot: bench/archon-13b/int8/batch4/ctx1024/run-1 complete. p50=48ms, p95=180ms, p99=420ms, tokens/s=5400, gpu_util=72%

anya: Good real numbers. p99 is higher than target at this config. Matt — can you rerun with warmup and KV-cache enabled, batch=4, concurrency=4? Also add a run with batching window=8ms and continuous batching off.

matt: On it. I'll queue variations and annotate runs with `warmup=true` and `kv_cache=on`. Also adding an experiment: micro-batch split where model processes 1 token at a time but networking batches (hoping to reduce p99).

jess: For evals I'll baseline int8/warm and run int4-smoke on a small shard to confirm no obvious regressions before full sweep. Will post diff table in thread.

sam: One more operational ask: capture GPU clocks and sm utilization per run. If we see sustained 95%+ util, we might have headroom to increase concurrency.

anya: Thanks team — action items: matt: create bench matrix + start runs; jess: prep eval shards and quality gating thresholds; sam: add warmup steps and kernel checks; I'll set up dashboard and incident thresholds (auto rollback if quality gate fails). Ping here when first warm/hot runs finish. :rocket:
